mainProgression.description: Classic I-IV-V power chord progression forming the backbone of the song

sectionProgressions.description: Modified progression with ♭VII adding rock edge and tension
Uses borrowed chords from parallel minor for heavier sound

harmonicFunction: B5 (I) - Establishes strong tonic center in B major
E5 (IV) - Provides subdominant movement and harmonic contrast
F#5 (V) - Creates dominant tension that resolves back to B5
A5 (♭VII) - Borrowed from B minor, adds classic rock character
G5 (♭VI) - Another borrowed chord creating darker harmonic color

techniques.name: B-String Open Pull-Off Riff & Alternate Picking Stamina
techniques.description: Angus Young's immortal 16th-note intro riff, rapidly alternating fretted notes with the ringing open B string across positions 4 to 12.

notes: B5: X-2-4-X-X-X (2nd fret A string + 4th fret D string)
E5: 0-2-2-X-X-X (Open E string + 2nd fret A and D strings)
F#5: 2-4-4-X-X-X (2nd fret low E string + 4th fret A and D strings)
Fretted notes on string 2: frets 4, 7, 5, 8, shifting up to 12, 10, 9, 7, 5, 4
Constant open B (string 2) pedal note
Played with strict alternate picking in the studio, or one-handed pull-offs live
sequence: Anchor your index finger on fret 4 of the B string and pinky on fret 7
Pick or hammer-pull between the fretted note and the open B string in strict 16th notes
Shift up to the 5th and 8th frets without losing the rhythmic pulse
Slide up to the 12th fret for the climactic descending run
tips: Although Angus famously mimed the intro one-handed in the video, producer Bruce Fairbairn confirmed it was alternate-picked in the studio for maximum punch
Rest your picking hand lightly on the lower strings (E, A, D, G) to prevent unwanted sympathetic vibration
Start at 90 BPM with a metronome and gradually build up to the track's relentless 133 BPM

techniques.name: Angus Young Blues-Metal Lead Solos & Malcolm Rhythm Engine
techniques.description: Channeling Angus's fiery 7th-position B minor and major pentatonic soloing style, featuring ferocious whole-step bends on the high E and B strings, screaming vibrato, and hyper-speed blues turnaround licks locked with Malcolm Young's unyielding Gretsch rhythm drive.

notes: 7th-position B minor pentatonic (B, D, E, F#, A) and B major pentatonic (B, C#, D#, F#, G#)
Whole-step bend on fret 10 string 1 (D up to E) with finger vibrato
Whole-step bend on fret 12 string 1 (E up to F#)
Cranked Marshall 100W Super Lead Plexi crunch with zero pedal distortion
sequence: Dig hard into fret 10 of the high E string with index-supported ring finger
Apply wide, singing finger vibrato while holding the bend at full pitch
Rip through descending blues pentatonic triplets across strings 2, 3, and 4
Conclude with an aggressive pick scrape sliding down the low strings into the riff
tips: Angus used a 1968 Gibson SG Standard with high-output bridge humbucker plugged straight into a cranked Marshall head
Malcolm's secret was light pick gauge on heavy strings, hitting open power chords with relentless downstrokes
Let the notes bite cleanly without excessive preamp gain—the punch comes from high volume and aggressive pick attack

sections.name: Thunderous Open B-String Hook
sections.description: Angus Young's immortal solo guitar intro alternating fretted notes with the ringing open B string in strict 16th notes.
notes: Maintain absolute rhythmic consistency at 133 BPM
Mute strings 3, 4, 5, and 6 to eliminate background rumble
Nail the shifting accents on the 12th-fret descent

sections.name: Full Band Entry & Thunder Chants
sections.description: Chris Slade's thunderous bass drum enters, followed by Malcolm Young's bone-crushing B5 power chord and the crowd chant 'THUNDER!'.
notes: Malcolm's seismic B5 chord entry on beat 1
Angus continues the relentless B-string 16th-note ostinato over the top
Hit the syncopated chord accents in lockstep with the bass drum

sections.name: Verse 1 Driving Pub-Rock Chug
sections.description: Brian Johnson's gritty vocal delivery over Malcolm's B5 - A5 - E5 - B5 rhythm bedrock with palm-muted driving downstrokes.
notes: Down-picking for maximum bite and aggression
Palm muting for a tight, chugged tone
Clean, authoritative chord transitions on every bar

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Climb & Thunder Stabs
sections.description: 'Sound of the drums, beatin' in my heart...' building tension through G5, D5, and A5 with sharp syncopated stabs.
notes: Full, ringing open power chords
Crisp dynamic build leading into the thunderous chorus hook
Accentuate beats 1 and 3

sections.name: Angus Young Blistering Guitar Solo
sections.technique: B Pentatonic Blues Bends & Rapid Triplets
sections.description: Angus's showstopping lead guitar solo in 7th-position B minor/major pentatonic with whole-step bends, hyper-speed blues pull-offs, and singing vibrato.
notes: Singing whole-step bend on fret 10 string 1 with aggressive finger vibrato
Rapid descending pentatonic runs through frets 9 and 7 on strings 2, 3, and 4
High whole-step bend on fret 12 string 1 peaking with stadium sustain

sections.name: Outro Anthem & Unstoppable Climax
sections.technique: High-Energy Rhythm Jam & Screaming Lead Fills
sections.description: The final breathless repeat of the Thunder chant, racing rhythm chords, and Angus's screaming lead fills concluding on an explosive final B5 hit.
notes: Power chord drive with maximum adrenaline
Angus throws in rapid B blues pentatonic screaming fills
Massive final downstroke choke on B5
